composition: Draft-first reading sheet with a horizontal 3D push tile rail and stepped acetate source leaves.
approvalBasis: User selected a blend of the 3D streaming title-card wall and the acetate reference manual, then directed the redesign to feel less AI-generated. This composition was chosen from the resulting three hybrid boards because it gives the draft and evidence the clearest reading order.
prompt: Third composition concept for the same ShipBrief hybrid visual world, 1440x960 desktop software screenshot. Keep exactly the same identity: streaming push tiles plus acetate reference-manual evidence, deep graphite, teal, warm ivory, clear acetate, tiny vermilion markers, dimensional 3D material and real shadows, high-end Shopify ecosystem app craft. Change only the composition: a narrow horizontal 3D push-tile rail spans below the top navigation, selected tile 'Update settings navigation' sits slightly raised; below, one large open ivory draft sheet fills the main 2/3 of the viewport as the focal area; the right margin is a vertical stepped rail of translucent acetate source tabs for linked commits, changed files, compare evidence, each tab hinging open on focus. Human review status and Edit / Approve controls anchor in a persistent bottom bar. Left sidebar has Overview, Drafts, Runs, Repositories, Workflows, Brand voice. Include visible LOCAL DEMO · SAMPLE DATA · NOT CONNECTED. The main sheet copy is conservative: 'Review the linked commits before sharing.' Tie one exact commit topic 'Update settings navigation' to its source tab. Show a single miniature 3D acetate leaf mid-hinge and the chosen push tile lifted, suggesting focused motion; no object/photo outside the UI, no room or desk. Clear task hierarchy, ample whitespace around the reading surface, working app controls remain crisp. No unsupported outcomes, no fake integrations or publishing, no generic panel soup, gradients, or glassmorphism except clear acetate as a named material. This composition should feel deliberately different from both a horizontal card wall over a split-detail view and a vertical card rail with a centered detail panel.
